title: SDK Integration Walkthrough (Python/TypeScript) - Quickstart & Auth
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Nimbus Labs through Python and TypeScript SDK quickstarts, auth patterns (API keys, env vars, OIDC), and basic Console flows. Discussed runtime choices (hosted vs dedicated), Optimize recommendations (batching, prefix caching), and next steps: share quickstart repo, security docs, benchmark script and schedule pilot kickoff.
action_items: Maya - Send quickstart repo (Python & TS) and sample notebooks - 2025-10-17
Carlos - Share sample benchmark script for embedding/response latency and recommended payloads - 2025-10-20
Priya - Provide current traffic profile and 95th percentile latency SLOs - 2025-10-18
Maya - Share SOC2/ISO security docs and private deployment checklist - 2025-10-17
next_steps: Schedule 1-hour pilot kickoff (AE/SE + Nimbus eng) - propose next Tue/Thu
Nimbus to send sample dataset and traffic profile for bench
Redwood to provide dedicated trial pricing and pilot agreement template
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll do a quick SDK walkthrough for Python and TypeScript, cover auth and quickstarts, and then show the Console and some Optimize tips.
[00:12] Alex (Nimbus): Great, thanks. We invited Priya and Samir from infra, we're mostly interested in embedding pipeline and chat latency.
[00:20] Carlos (Redwood SE): Awesome, quick intro from me — I usually run the SDKs and benchmarks, I'll share a small script you can run locally. Quick question: do you plan to use hosted Redwood or Dedicated capacity?
[00:34] Priya (Nimbus): Likely hosted to start, but we may need Dedicated in 6-9 months for steady throughput. Also curious about on-prem eventually.
[00:44] Maya: Totally reasonable. Today we'll show hosted flow, but I'll note the Dedicated/private bits when we hit security.
[00:51] Carlos: Alright jumping into code. For Python we have pip package redwood-inference (note: our internal naming may appear as redwood-sdk in some places in the docs, small discrepancy in auto gen). Installation is pip install redwood-inference. For TypeScript: npm i @redwood/inference or yarn add @redwood/inference.
[01:10] Samir (Nimbus SRE): Quick q: how do you recommend storing the API key? env var or secrets manager?
[01:15] Maya: Best practice -> env var for local dev, and use your cloud KMS or secrets manager in prod. We also support OIDC-based auth and short-lived tokens if you need tighter rotation. I'll share the OIDC config doc.
[01:28] Carlos: Example Python snippet:

from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
resp = client.generate('Write a short product blurb about Nimbus Labs')
print(resp.text)

[01:48] (audio noise)
[01:50] Priya: A tiny transcription note: we saw redwood-inference referenced but our package manager flagged @redwood/inference. We'll use the repo you send.
[01:58] Carlos: Yup we'll include both references and the repo links. For TypeScript quickstart:

import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
const res = await client.chat.create({ model: 'rw-large-1', messages: [...] })
console.log(res.choices[0].text)

[02:20] Alex: Nice. About models — do you expose model variants for quantized/low-cost runs?
[02:24] Maya: Yes, we have curated model catalog. You can pin a high-accuracy model or an optimized quantized variant. For many embedding-heavy workloads we'll recommend a smaller quantized model to reduce cost.
[02:35] Carlos: On the SDK, there's also a streaming helper which uses SSE for token-by-token updates, and a built-in retry/backoff. We'll show the Console route for toggling streaming.
[02:47] Priya: For envs, what about URL and region? Do we set an endpoint or does the client auto-resolve?
[02:53] Carlos: By default client auto-resolves to hosted endpoint in your nearest region, but you can override with an endpoint parameter for private deployments or to target dedicated. Example: Client({ endpoint: 'https://us-east-1.api.redwood.ai' }).
[03:05] Alex: Good. Can you show the Console auth UI so our infra team can review token rotation?
[03:10] Maya: Sure — switching to the Console. (screen share) In the Console under Settings > API Keys you can create scoped keys (read-only, embeddings-only, full). We also have short-lived session tokens via OIDC integration; you'll see Add IdP in the Security tab.
[03:28] Samir: Does Redwood integrate with our existing SSO (Okta)?
[03:31] Maya: Yes Okta, Azure AD, Ping — SAML/OIDC supported. We'll share the SSO setup doc.
[03:37] Carlos: Back to code — quick note on batching: the Python SDK has a batch helper for embeddings which will pad and batch natively to reduce overhead. The Optimize recommendations will also suggest batch sizes based on your average sequence length.
[03:52] Priya: Does Optimize automatically change batch sizes or just recommend?
[03:55] Maya: Recommend only. We provide safe defaults and a suggested config you can apply. For Dedicated we can automate more aggressive batching with customer approval.
[04:05] Alex: Can we see an example of setting headers and troubleshooting auth errors?
[04:09] Carlos: Sure. Common error is 401 when REDWOOD_API_KEY is missing or malformed. For Node we do: headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}` }. If using OIDC, you'll exchange the OIDC token for a short-lived Redwood session token; the Console has an exchange endpoint. We'll include the curl example.
[04:29] Priya: About telemetry and PII — how much of our prompt content is logged?
[04:33] Maya: For hosted, by default we retain logs for 30 days for debugging, can be configured per-contract. Enterprise/private options allow zero retention and customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS). We'll attach the data retention matrix.
[04:46] Carlos: Quick demo of a simple benchmark script: we run batches of 16 for embeddings and report mean/95p latency. We'll send the script; it uses the SDK batch helper and a payload generator.
[04:59] (typing)
[05:05] Alex: From a success criterion standpoint: we need 200qps sustained with 95p latency under 250ms for chat. Is that something Redwood can hit on hosted?
[05:17] Maya: Hosted can get close depending on model and config; typically for strict SLA we recommend Dedicated. We'll propose pilot numbers and run benchmark with your payload to confirm.
[05:30] Carlos: Also note that prefix/KV caching can dramatically reduce per-token latency for chat if you have repetitive system/preamble content.
[05:40] Priya: Great. For TypeScript SDK patterns — do you have typed responses or is it free-form?
[05:45] Carlos: We return a typed object shape in TS SDK (Choice[], usage, tokens). For structured output we support JSON schema enforcement and function/tool-calling patterns.
[05:56] Alex: Can you show an example of embeddings pipeline with vector DB?
[06:00] Carlos: Sure — quick pseudo: generate embeddings via client.embeddings.create({ model:'rw-embed-1', input: [...] }) then send to your vector DB. Our helper returns a flattened vector array. We'll include a sample for Pinecone and Milvus.
[06:14] Samir: Are there rate limits on hosted?
[06:17] Maya: Yes soft limits by default, configurable on paid plans. For pilot we'll bump limits. We'll include rate limit guidance in the doc.
[06:25] Priya: For the quickstart repo, can we get a Docker example to run the benchmark reproducibly?
[06:30] Carlos: Yup we'll include Docker + GitHub Actions for CI.
[06:34] (brief pause)
[06:37] Alex: Security review: audit logs and SIEM integration — do you push logs?
[06:41] Maya: We provide audit logs export to S3 and webhook hooks for SIEM ingestion; Retention policy and access controls in enterprise plans.
[06:50] Carlos: Back to SDK: error handling pattern — 429s will include Retry-After header, we provide an exponential backoff util; we'll include snippet. Also token refresh flows for OIDC are in the docs.
[07:05] Priya: Any gotchas for bundlers and tree-shaking in TS?
[07:09] Carlos: Use the ESM entrypoint, and keep import from '@redwood/inference/esm' if you need smaller bundles. We'll note this in the README. Small transcription: sometimes docs reference redwood-js in early drafts.
[07:22] Alex: About cost: do you break down by model and tokens in Console?
[07:26] Maya: Yes Console usage tab shows per-model token breakdown and per-route cost. You can set quotas and alerts.
[07:33] Carlos: We'll also show how to pin routes to cheaper model variants during off-peak hours via routing policies.
[07:40] Priya: For the pilot, we'd like a canary rollout and traffic split. Is that supported?
[07:44] Maya: Yep Canary/A-B and automatic fallbacks if a model becomes overloaded. We'll show a sample rollout config.
[07:52] (screen share switches back to code)
[08:00] Carlos: Now I'll run the local quickstart — stepping through: clone repo, pip install -r requirements, export REDWOOD_API_KEY, python run_quickstart.py. The script sends a chat request and prints tokens/time.
[08:18] (script runs)
[08:22] Carlos: Example output: 1 request, 120ms median, 180ms p95 (dev region).
[08:29] Alex: That's encouraging.
[08:31] Priya: What's typical for embeddings?
[08:33] Carlos: Embeddings batch of 16 in dev: ~70ms mean, 120ms p95 per batch for rw-embed-1. Quantized small embed models can be faster.
[08:44] Samir: When you send the benchmark script, please include expected environment (Python 3.10, node 18, etc).
[08:50] Maya: We'll include full env matrix.
[08:55] Alex: Any limits around prompt length or context windows?
[08:59] Carlos: Context window is model-dependent, rw-large-1 is 8k by default, we support extended variants. We also have streaming for long outputs.
[09:09] Priya: For compliance, can we bring our own KMS?
[09:12] Maya: Yes BYOK supported in Private/Dedicated and available as an add-on in some contracts. We'll include steps.
[09:19] (slight cross talk)
[09:23] Carlos: One more SDK tip — the client supports a local mock mode for unit tests so you don't call the API on CI. We'll add that to the repo.
[09:33] Maya: Ok wrapping up with next steps. I'll send the quickstart repo, SOC2/ISO docs, and a proposed pilot pricing sheet. Carlos will share benchmark script and Docker example. Nimbus to provide traffic profile and sample dataset.
[09:48] Alex: Sounds good. Can we do a pilot kickoff next Wednesday?
[09:52] Maya: We'll propose Wednesday and Thursday slots.
[09:55] (end of main content, some small chatter)
[10:00] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with links.
[44:30] (call ends)
